summary: 16 active modules across 5 rooms. All module handlers are real (graduated from stubs). Partner is feature-flagged off by default but ships with hardcoded fake signals. Care Circle and Garden are design-only (zero code). WidgetKit infrastructure is written but no Swift extension target exists. Language setting has no UI caller. Key gaps: onboarding missing, language picker missing, goals progress arc is a fake, pets species hardcoded to guinea_pig for all users, pets coregulation log never written.
mismatch: Partner module: all 3 rounds agree the feature is UI-complete and flag-gated OFF, and that SAMPLE_SIGNALS is a live data fixture. No dissent — unanimous confirmed bug.
Language picker: Rounds 1 and 2 confirm zero callers. Round 3 did not independently cover this finding but did not contradict it.
Goals arc: all 3 rounds agree it is fake. No dissent.
Onboarding: Rounds 1 and 2 confirm absence. Round 3 confirmed moduleManifest personal names separately. Combined picture is consistent.

Pets species hardcoding and coregulation gap: only Round 3 found these — Round 1 and Round 2 did not inspect pets/bridge.ts. Confidence 1, but code evidence is direct (BUILD GAP comment + zero write grep). Not contradicted by other rounds.
JournalNoticed: only Round 1 found this. Rounds 2 and 3 did not contradict it — Round 1 cites an explicit 'not yet built' comment in dump/index.ts.

summary: The Ollie monorepo has a consistent pattern of orphaned packages, dead notification backends, split API layers, and a mis-wired cadence-scanner notification path. The most critical issues are: (1) the cadence-scanner fires all time-based cues to a NOOP console backend — no device notification ever reaches the user from this path; (2) three parallel module-name registries diverge silently and cause silent routing drops; (3) apps/api (ollie-notifications worker) is undeployed with a placeholder KV ID yet is the hardcoded target for iOS device-token registration; (4) three packages (@ollie/sync, @ollie/auth, @ollie/research-stream) are fully orphaned but CI still builds and tests them, creating false confidence that encrypted sync and passphrase vault are live.
mismatch: cadence-scanner→NOOP: Code confirms notify() goes to NOOP_BACKEND, but store.ts comment ('scanner calls notify() internally regardless') may indicate intentional in-app-UI-only delivery. Needs device-level runtime verification before treating as confirmed P1.

@ollie/sync: Architecture docs and CI claim encrypted Supabase sync is the user-data transport, but code shows the native app writes plaintext to SQLite with no @ollie/sync import anywhere. Sync may be intentionally deferred (VITE_SERVER_APPLY flag) or silently regressed — unverified at runtime.

apps/api deploy state: wrangler.toml comment says 'NOT currently deployed' but this cannot be confirmed without running `wrangler deployments list --name ollie-notifications`. If it was manually deployed at some point, the KV placeholder may be live.

packages/notifications backend enforcement: Round 1 says constitutional rules are 'enforced by type definitions only, not at runtime'. Round 3 confirms NOOP path. No round found a runtime path where budget or dedupe actually fires on device — consistent, but no positive runtime confirmation.

angle: Agent 3 — Frontend App Architecture (apps/native/src, React/Tauri shell, routing, state, module/room wiring). Branch: redesign/olive-neumorphic.
summary: Three independent rounds inspected the same codebase section and converged on 11 distinct issues. The two highest-risk structural gaps are: (1) zero error boundary coverage — any uncaught render throw white-screens the entire app with no recovery; and (2) useModuleData silently swallowing SQLite errors, leaving users on an infinite loading dot. Both were confirmed across all three rounds. A third systemic risk — the COMPONENTS registry typed as non-nullable masking undefined at runtime — was found by Round 3 and is a P2 crash trap. Dark mode infrastructure exists but is architecturally frozen by 40 files using a static color import; this is intentional today (forceMode=light) but will require a large-scale port when unblocked. Duplicate inline style constants (SMCP_STYLE/KICKER_STYLE/TITLE_STYLE) and Tile component copies are cosmetic debt confirmed across all three rounds. Quick-win dead code (App.tsx stub) and minor UX regressions (blank Clerk loading, hardcoded greeting, pets orphan in IA) round out the picture.
mismatch: Dark mode: ThemeProvider + CSS vars are fully implemented and would work for 7 CSS Module files, but 40 inline-style files import a static `colors` alias — so dark mode works in CSS but is frozen in inline styles. forceMode='light' intentionally gates this. Not a mismatch per se, but the system appears to support dark mode while being architecturally incapable of it for most screens.

navigate(-1) in BackBar: Round 3 flags this as P3/suspected because Tauri WKWebView may behave differently from a standard browser on empty history stack. Rounds 1 and 2 noted the same pattern but did not flag it as a distinct issue. Actual behavior on device is unverified.

GrocerySyncBridge getToken stability: All three rounds note that Clerk v5 documents getToken as a stable reference, but none could verify this in the Tauri localhost proxy context at static analysis time. Needs runtime confirmation.

angle: Backend/API Architecture — workers/ai-proxy, apps/api, workers/cron, workers/apns-push, packages/worker-http
summary: The ai-proxy worker exposes two unauthenticated Anthropic API proxy endpoints (/brain-dump and /v1/messages) that are rate-limited only by a spoofable client-supplied header, creating direct financial exposure. A misleading wrangler.toml queue binding comment masks an either-deploy-breaking-or-double-processing defect. Several lower-severity analytic, rate-limit, and auth issues round out the picture.
mismatch: Finding #2 (wrangler.toml queue bindings): comment says 'intentionally left commented' but the TOML block is uncommented and active. Cannot determine from static analysis whether the queue is provisioned in CF — runtime check (`wrangler queues list`) required to pick the correct fix branch.

Finding #3 (cacheHitUpdate hit_count): route.test.ts mocks the PATCH to 204 without validating the body — the test passes while the production call silently fails with a 400 type error on every cache hit. Implementation says 'increment' but runtime PostgREST ignores it.

Finding #13 (upstreamError errText leak): Round 3 suspected a client-facing leak. Direct code read of packages/worker-http/src/index.ts confirms errText is logged server-side only and stripped from client responses. Round 3 dissent resolved: this is NOT a live vulnerability.

summary: The database layer has three clusters of critical problems: (1) GDPR/account-delete is mechanically broken — the JWT verifier calls a Supabase Auth endpoint that rejects Clerk JWTs, so every deletion attempt returns 401, and even if fixed, 5 Clerk-user-scoped tables are absent from the cascade list; (2) the identity model is split — profiles still carries a uuid FK to auth.users and all its RLS policies use auth.uid() which returns NULL under Clerk, making the table inert for all current users and breaking cross-device salt roaming silently; (3) multiple schema-level defects (dead RLS policies, missing CHECK constraint value, no tombstone purge, no unpair cleanup, LWW timestamp manipulation vector) compound these core problems.
mismatch: account-delete.ts JWT verifier (calls Supabase /auth/v1/user) vs. Clerk-issued JWTs in production: tests pass (mocked) but live calls return 401 — complete runtime breakage masked by mock
profiles RLS policies use auth.uid() which is NULL under Clerk JWT: schema appears functional in static review but is permanently denied at runtime for all Clerk users
grocery_purchase_history self-select RLS: policy text looks plausible (auth.uid()::text = user_id) but evaluates to NULL/false at runtime because Clerk JWT does not populate auth.uid()
routing_cache HNSW index: schema review shows an index exists, but at runtime pgvector ANN search does not respect the post-filter WHERE module = $1, enabling cross-module cache hits
routing_cache CHECK constraint vs MODULE_CONFIGS in route.ts: 'medication' is a valid routable module in TypeScript but is absent from the SQL constraint, causing silent INSERT failures at runtime

summary: The auth layer has two P0/P1 compliance failures and a cluster of P2 defense-in-depth gaps. The most critical: account-delete.ts uses Supabase-only JWT verification but all current users authenticate via Clerk, meaning every real delete request returns 401 and user data is never actually erased — a clear GDPR/App Store violation. The /brain-dump and /v1/messages endpoints are unauthenticated Anthropic proxies that anyone can hit to drain the API key. Rate-limit enforcement is broken on multiple paths (null-skip, spoofable x-user-id header, missing bindings on invite endpoints). A legacy Supabase auth fallback has no sunset mechanism. Clerk JWT verification omits the audience claim. A draft security-invoker migration for invite_funnel views was written but never applied to prod.
mismatch: wrangler.toml comment on validate-invite/claim-invite says 'rely on per-IP CF rate limit' but no [[ratelimits]] binding exists for these paths — comment is factually false

packages/auth/src/index.ts comment says the package no longer does Supabase Auth, but supabase/migrations/20260518000001 still grants anon SELECT on profiles for the old Supabase new-device flow — code and DB schema are out of sync
DEPLOY_TODO.md references VITE_USER_HASH_SALT but the worker env var is USER_HASH_SALT — naming mismatch means the deploy checklist may not ensure the correct secret is set
account-delete.ts USER_SCOPED_TABLES was not updated after the 20260522–20260618 migration wave that added 7 new user-scoped tables — table inventory and code are out of sync

summary: Security audit of Ollie monorepo (branch redesign/olive-neumorphic). Three rounds inspected workers/ai-proxy, workers/sentry-tunnel, apps/native (Tauri/React), packages/crypto, packages/notifications, supabase/migrations, and .env files. All critical findings are code-confirmed. Runtime gaps (migration application status, deployed wrangler secrets) flagged where applicable.
mismatch: Migration 20260618000002 (Clerk-text identity fix for auth.uid()→NULL) is present in the repo but cannot be confirmed as applied to the production Supabase instance from files alone — requires `supabase db diff` or migration history table check by Serra.

T0_JWT_ENFORCED value in the live deployed ai-proxy wrangler secrets is unknown — if set to '0' in prod, /route/:module and /transcribe endpoints would also be unauthenticated. Requires `wrangler secret list --name ollie-ai-proxy`.

USER_HASH_SALT: wrangler.toml has no record of this secret being set, and the telemetry.ts warn log fires when absent — runtime check via `wrangler secret list` needed to confirm whether it was ever set on the deployed worker.
VITE_USER_HASH_SALT: grep of apps/native/src returns zero references, suggesting Vite does NOT inline it into the bundle today — but a post-build grep of dist/ is needed to confirm definitively.

profile_recovery_lookup anon EXECUTE grant: confirmed live in the migration SQL (line 111). Whether a subsequent migration has revoked it is unknown — no later migration in the inspected set touches this grant.
STAGING_TEST_BEARER: whether this secret is inadvertently set on the production worker cannot be determined from files alone — requires `wrangler secret list` against the prod worker.

profiles table uuid↔Clerk deletion: account-delete.ts line 125 shows the profiles row deletion using uuid column — whether the Clerk→uuid translation actually resolves at deletion time requires a live account-delete integration test to confirm.

summary: Independent static-code audit of privacy and sensitive data handling across the Ollie monorepo (branch redesign/olive-neumorphic). Covers: consent enforcement, data collection flows (/enrich-dump, /label, research pipeline), encryption at rest and in transit, analytics/Sentry, deletion/retention, PII scrub coverage, partner crisis data, and account deletion gaps. All three rounds inspected overlapping file sets; findings were confirmed against source files directly.
mismatch: enrichDump() is exported from apps/native/src/api/workers.ts and api/index.ts but has ZERO call sites in app code — the research pipeline is currently dead-code. Round 1 and Round 2 flag this as a 'pre-wiring risk'; Round 3 independently confirms no callers. The server-side /enrich-dump endpoint with no consent gate is a structural gap that will become a live violation the moment anyone wires the call site.

@ollie/consent configureConsent() is never called in the app (confirmed by grep). Round 3 notes this means the research gate permanently returns false (research pipeline silently dead); Rounds 1 and 2 describe it as 'bypassed'. The net effect differs: currently the gate denies by sentinel, but the structural wiring is absent, meaning a single call to configureConsent() without a consent UI would flip the gate open invisibly.

encryptedKv exists at apps/native/src/storage/encrypted.ts but grep finds zero callers in apps/native/src — the encrypted storage layer is implemented but completely unwired. All module data goes through the plaintext browserAdapter path.

summary: Three rounds inspected ai-proxy, apns-push, apps/api, and native module handlers. The dominant pattern: field-level validation is inconsistently applied — some routes have thorough guards (feed-me, partner, purchase) while neighbouring routes in the same file were missed. One P1 auth hole (/brain-dump open Anthropic proxy) and one P1 prompt-injection path (/label locale interpolated into Anthropic user message) are the headline risks. Below those: dumpId KV key overflow, unbounded metadata strings in enrich-dump, missing Content-Length pre-checks on two routes, and several minor format-validation gaps. All findings are code-confirmed; no runtime verification was needed.
mismatch: /route/dump locale: R1 says bad locale can cause a 500 (RangeError in some V8 versions, dump lost); R2 rates it P4 and says try/catch in segmentation.ts lines 89-98 handles it gracefully; R3 confirms the try/catch exists. Resolution: the fallback is real but V8-version-dependent behaviour is unverified at runtime — treat as P3 with defensive fix still warranted.

CF KV key 512-byte limit for dumpId overflow (Finding 3): all three rounds describe the overflow but whether CF Workers platform silently truncates or throws needs runtime verification. R1 says KV.put .catch() is silent; R2 confirms caught+non-crashing; R3 agrees. The silent failure path is consistent across rounds but actual CF platform behaviour is unconfirmed without wrangler dev test.

summary: UI/UX audit of apps/native/src on branch redesign/olive-neumorphic. Covers dump flow, room navigation, module reachability, copy quality, empty/error states, accessibility, onboarding, dark mode, and ADHD-safety fidelity. All findings code-confirmed; no runtime verification performed.
mismatch: prefers-reduced-motion: Rounds 2 and 3 mark ack animation as 'correctly implemented' in doNotTouch; Round 1 correctly identifies that opacity:1 with animation-duration:0ms still produces a 2.5s solid-colour viewport block for reduced-motion users — the CSS intent (no animation) is achieved but the UX outcome (no jarring colour flood) is not.

Mood module reachability: Round 2 flags MoodBox as P2 unreachable. HealthRoom.tsx comment (line 353) says 'there's no mood screen' and the energy tile is explicitly READ-ONLY by design. Whether this is a product decision or an omission is unresolved — needs product verification before treating as a bug.

GoalCreateModal 5-field requirement: Rounds 1 and 2 flag as P2 ADHD blocker. Project memory (project_ollie_goals_rich_capture.md) records this as a deliberate design decision (required fields at creation for Ulysses-contract integrity). The bug vs feature status is a product call, but the UX impact on ADHD users is real regardless of intent.

angle: Agent 11 — Design System & Frontend Code Quality
summary: The olive-neumorphic design system has two structural blockers before Faz 6b (dark mode) can ship: (1) 40+ production files import the static `colors = lightPalette` alias instead of the reactive theme hook, and (2) all neumorphic shadow tokens hardcode white highlight values. Beyond dark mode, the Input primitive is silently unstyled due to ~14 undefined CSS variable names, DM Sans 300 weight is never loaded, and the type scale is bypassed by 139–158 raw fontSize integers across modules. Deduplication and copy-paste drift are pervasive: SMCP/kicker styles exist in 5–13 independent copies with diverging letterSpacing values, and the inset shadow string is duplicated 13–15 times with three different blur radii. Quick wins exist (paper-2 CSS var typo, App.css dead-code deletion, font weight import) that are single-line or near-zero risk.
mismatch: R3 marked App.css as dead code (App.tsx not imported by main.tsx) but R2 said it is 'live in the CSS cascade' — R3 is correct per grep evidence; App.css has no runtime effect currently.

R3 flagged `var(--ollie-color-paper-2)` in Button.module.css as 'looks correct by camelToKebab rule' (missingInfo) while R2 ran the actual transform and confirmed it is broken. R2 evidence is definitive — the var is broken in production.

R1 framed the neumorphic white shadow issue as part of the inline duplication finding (P2); R2 and R3 elevated it to a standalone structural problem (P1-adjacent) because it affects the shadow token definitions themselves, not just inline copies. Merged as separate P1 finding.

summary: The test suite has solid unit coverage in isolated domains (crypto, sync LWW, crisis-lexicon, dump-classifier) but has three structural CI holes that let regressions ship silently: (1) deploy-workers.yml fires to production in parallel with ci.yml with no blocking dependency, (2) coverage thresholds in orchestrator/vitest.config.ts are never executed in CI, and (3) the client-side crisis safety wiring is untested end-to-end. Beyond CI structure, the partner module (consent/interpret/pairing routes) and brain/actions.ts action dispatch are almost entirely untested despite being privacy-sensitive and user-trust-critical flows.
mismatch: Partner consent filtering: interpret.ts is code-confirmed as the consent gate, but zero tests exist — there is no runtime verification that the flags default to 'no share' rather than 'share'. If the default is inverted (share-by-default), a runtime user would expose data without knowing it, but CI would never surface this.

Rate-limit key extraction: tests run with JWT enforcement disabled (T0_JWT_ENFORCED='0') while production runs with it enabled. The two code paths produce different rate-key sources (JWT sub vs x-user-id header). A bug in the JWT path is invisible to the test suite.

Coverage thresholds: vitest.config.ts documents thresholds as 'enforced in CI' but the script chain proves they never run. The comment and reality are inverted — teams reading the config believe coverage is gated when it is not.

deploy-workers.yml: the intent (test before deploy) is implied by having tests at all, but the implementation deploys concurrently with testing. Any developer who pushes a breaking change to main assumes tests would block the deploy — they do not.

summary: The Ollie monorepo has a two-tier CI blind spot: CF workers deploy to production without any quality gate, and the entire Rust/Tauri codebase is never compiled in CI. The banned-phrase scanner is hollow (scans ghost paths, misses 281+ active UI files). CSP is disabled in the production Tauri config. Three independent rounds converged on 5 of the 12 findings with confidence 3, and all major findings are corroborated by at least 2 rounds.
mismatch: tauri-plugin-localhost on iOS: Cargo.toml and lib.rs show unconditional initialization (Round 2 suspected, Round 3 did not flag it, Round 1 did not flag it). iOS build artifacts in Cargo.lock suggest it compiles, but runtime behavior of a TCP localhost server inside an iOS app process is unverified. Flagged as suspected by Round 2 only — needs device smoke-test.

ESLint no-banned-copy rule: Round 1 says it covers apps/native (mitigating the scanner gap); Round 2 confirms this; Round 3 confirms but notes JSON files are not covered by ESLint. All three agree ESLint is the real guard, but no round verified pnpm lint passes cleanly today — it has never been runtime-verified in CI output.

gen/apple committed to git: Round 2 flagged this as P3; Rounds 1 and 3 both note gen/apple in doNotTouch as intentionally committed for Xcode workflow. Dissent: Round 2 argues it should be gitignored (auto-generated), but Round 3 says it is committed intentionally. Needs product decision on whether gen/apple is hand-edited.

summary: The Ollie monorepo has a cascade of deployment infrastructure gaps that range from guaranteed CI failures to silent production contamination. The most critical are: queue bindings declared active in wrangler.toml despite the comment saying they are commented out (any push to workers/ hard-fails CI deploy); deploy-workers.yml runs in parallel with ci.yml with no dependency, so broken tests never gate production deploys; and staging and production share identical KV namespace IDs, meaning staging test traffic writes into prod routing cache. Secondary risks include 18 of 39 migrations with no rollback scripts, an auth bypass that activates when ENVIRONMENT is unset rather than requiring an explicit staging opt-in, and iOS build numbers already drifted across three files. All findings are confirmed by direct file inspection on branch redesign/olive-neumorphic.
mismatch: workers/ai-proxy/wrangler.toml comment says [[queues.producers]] is 'COMMENTED OUT' but the binding is live TOML — comment and code disagree (all 3 rounds confirmed).
workers/cron/wrangler.toml same mismatch: comment says 'COMMENTED OUT' but [[queues.consumers]] is active.

STAGING_TEST_BEARER guard in server-apply-routes.ts line 44 is documented as a staging-only bypass but activates on any non-'production' ENVIRONMENT value including undefined — the test at line 154 explicitly verifies the bypass works when ENVIRONMENT is unset, which is the risky path.

workers/sentry-tunnel/src/index.ts implements TUNNEL_RATE_LIMITER interface and documents it as a security control ('per-IP fixed-window rate limit (429)'), but wrangler.toml has no [[ratelimits]] binding — the security control is effectively absent in production.

Supabase migration 20260618000004 is marked 'DRAFT — NOT yet applied to prod' in the file header, meaning security_invoker_views RLS fix documented as done in audit reports may not actually be live in the production database.

summary: The dump-and-routing pipeline has three compounding failures that make it effectively non-functional as a fast path: (1) cacheHitBump destroys Vectorize entries on first hit by omitting createdAt, making the entire cache a one-shot; (2) PostgREST hit_count increment is silently a no-op in both route.ts and feed-me.ts; (3) pass-2 segmentation and the cron drain both run serial Groq/Anthropic calls that can push total latency past 15–50 seconds. Layered on top: no fetch timeouts on any upstream API call, a 6-second unconditional SQLite polling loop on 37+ screens, no code splitting for the 14-module bundle, and the Groq free-tier TPM ceiling that collapses under 2 concurrent users. The Vectorize eviction sweep (CAP_PER_USER=10,000) is also dead code — never invoked from any cron job.
mismatch: GROQ_MODEL='openai/gpt-oss-120b': all three rounds flag this as suspected-invalid but cannot confirm without a live Groq API call. admin.config.ts uses valid Groq model IDs (llama-3.1-8b-instant) for the fast tier but the accurate-tier constant uses an OpenRouter-style path. Needs `curl /openai/v1/models` verification before triaging as bug vs. intentional alias.

Vectorize eviction: Round 1 noted eviction score logic is architecturally sound. Round 3 confirmed it is dead code. No dissent on the dead-code finding, but there is disagreement on whether it matters now (Round 1: 'not yet a problem at free tier cap', Round 3: 'old misclassified entries poison cache precision'). The P1 cacheHitBump bug makes this moot in the short term — entries self-destruct anyway.

routing_cache hit_count: All three rounds agree it is silently broken. Round 3 additionally notes there is no stored procedure for atomic increment in any migration file, confirming the fix requires a new SQL function or RPC — not just a client-side change.

summary: The ai-proxy Cloudflare Worker is the integration hub for Clerk JWT auth, Supabase, Voyage embeddings, Groq/Gemini/CF-AI/OpenRouter cascade, APNs push, Sentry tunnel, and CF Queues. Round 1 produced no findings. Rounds 2 and 3 are in strong agreement on all major issues. Three P1s stand out: /brain-copy has no rate limit (flagged in the 2026-06-18 audit and still unfixed), CF Queues TOML blocks are live despite comments saying they should be commented out (deploy bomb), and Voyage is a single embedding-layer SPOF with no fallback. Additional P2s cover unsalted telemetry user hashes, stale Supabase JWT fallback never removed after Clerk migration, APNs JWT cache not keyed on keyId, missing GEMINI_API_KEY and OPENROUTER_API_KEY in secrets docs, and unauthenticated requests bypassing rate limiting before getting 401. P3s cover Sentry being dead infrastructure and Groq model pricing having unverified constants.
mismatch: CF Queues TOML blocks: prose comments say 'COMMENTED OUT' but the TOML is live — actual queue provisioning state in Cloudflare cannot be determined from source alone; requires `wrangler queues list` to resolve
USER_HASH_SALT: not in wrangler.toml docs but could be set via `wrangler secret put` — status 'suspected' not 'confirmed'; requires CF dashboard inspection to confirm

Groq model 'openai/gpt-oss-120b': appeared after August 2025 knowledge cutoff; cannot confirm it is a valid Groq model ID from source alone; requires `curl https://api.groq.com/openai/v1/models` to resolve

summary: Covers the dump routing pipeline (Layer 1/2), crisis detection, confidence policy, Vectorize cache lifecycle, module classification validation, replenishment/cadence logic, noticing selection scoring, and the learning loop across the Ollie monorepo (branch redesign/olive-neumorphic). All three rounds inspected the same core files; findings converge on three structural problems: (1) crisis tier-1 false-positives causing silent dump loss, (2) unreviewed safety-critical lexicons with no CI gate, and (3) multiple cache/validation gaps that silently corrupt routing data.
mismatch: dump.ts comment line 15 says 'tier ≥ 2' for crisis short-circuit but code at line 302 checks `if (crisis)` (any tier) — all three rounds confirm this mismatch

Module comment in packages/crisis-lexicon/src/index.ts:16 declares PENDING_SERRA_APPROVAL as an alpha blocker, but the app is already installed on device with no CI gate — self-declared gate is inoperative

cacheHitBump is documented as a 'bump' (preserve entry, update hit count) but CF Vectorize upsert semantics replace metadata entirely — the bump deletes createdAt, turning a popularity signal into an expiry trigger

hit_count PATCH uses {increment:1} object syntax which PostgREST does not support for int columns — documented in two prior audit rounds (docs/audit/2026-06-18/round-2.md, round-3.md) but still not fixed; the feature exists in code but is permanently non-functional at runtime
hasConjunction in segmentation.ts is computed from already-split parts — always false at runtime, making the documented 'prevent pass-2 on still-compound fragments' guard a no-op

selectNoticings thresholdFor('high') is documented as a capacity-aware scoring adjustment but returns the same value as 'medium' — Round 1 flagged it as intentional product design; Round 3 confirmed it as a dead branch; the code fact is agreed upon, the intent is ambiguous

angle: Agent 18 — Dead Code, Duplication & Reinvented Wheels
summary: The Ollie monorepo carries a large belt of dead and duplicated code accumulated across multiple architecture pivots. The most severe issue is a P0 GDPR/App Store compliance gap: the only account-deletion endpoint lives in an undeployed legacy worker (apps/api), meaning user erasure requests silently fail. Below that, three P2 issues carry real data-leakage or wasted-compute risk: Turkish/Spanish names reach Anthropic unredacted because 5 of 6 ai-proxy routes import the weaker local pii.ts instead of the canonical @ollie/pii-scrub; the void:braindump:submitted event is never emitted from the native app, so 9 orchestrator per-dump optimization handlers are permanently dark; and the burhan (olive-tree game) orchestrator runs on every boot writing store keys that no UI ever reads. Beyond those, roughly 3,400 lines of dead logic (predict, consumption, corrections, astrology, ritual, prompts, research-stream, braindump-dispatch, routeViaHaiku) compile and test on every CI run for zero production utility. Duplication is systematic: two PII scrubbers, two brand lists, three queue implementations, three retry policies, three newId() copies, and a local json() helper in apns-push that @ollie/worker-http already exports. Quick wins (one-file import swaps) can close several of these in under an hour.
mismatch: void:braindump:submitted: 9 orchestrator handlers are wired and tested in unit tests but the event is never emitted from the native app — handler code appears functional in tests but is permanently dark in production

research-stream / research orchestrator: both compile, both have passing tests, both appear functional — but neither is instantiated in any live boot path; the GDPR consent UI may surface a research opt-in that the backend never fulfills

braindump-dispatch.ts: re-exported from orchestrator/src/index.ts as if it is live API surface; appears to be the routing system from its exports but is never called by any app or worker in the current architecture

burhan orchestrator: wired into createOrchestrator and runs on every boot (implementation present), but the UI layer (BurhanBox, room registration) is entirely absent — the feature exists at the orchestrator layer but not the presentation layer
account deletion (apps/api): 385-line implementation exists and compiles but is absent from deploy pipeline — 100% implementation, 0% reachability in production

summary: The documentation layer of the Ollie monorepo is severely stale across every major doc. README.md, CODEBASE_MAP.md, DATA_SCHEMA.md, DEPLOY_TODO.md, and IOS_SETUP.md all describe architectures, commands, bundle IDs, or product names that are factually wrong. The app moved from Electron+Capacitor+apps/web to Tauri+apps/native months ago, but no doc was updated. Three runbook errors (wrong product name, wrong bundle ID, wrong command) will cause an operator to either test the wrong app, sign for the wrong bundle ID, or get a white screen during iOS installation. All fixes are documentation-only and zero-risk.
mismatch: consent_audit table: DATA_SCHEMA.md describes it as a live audit log, but Round 2 found no call sites in apps/native/src/ that call ingestEvent with table='consent_audit'. Whether GDPR consent rows are ever written is unverified at runtime — needs `grep -rn 'ingestEvent' apps/native/src/ | grep consent` + live Supabase row count.

Plaid tables (plaid_items/plaid_inbox): code says removed, migrations say present, account-delete.ts sweeps them. Whether the tables exist and are empty in production Supabase is unknown without a live query. If they don't exist, account-delete throws at those lines on every user deletion.

USER_HASH_SALT worker secret: DEPLOY_TODO instructs setting a VITE_* client-side var with no effect. Whether the actual worker secret was ever set via wrangler is unknown — if unset, telemetry hashes are unsalted (workers/ai-proxy/src/telemetry.ts line 47 warns but continues).

App Group / group_container.rs GROUP_ID: IOS_SETUP.md and code use com.ollie.app prefix but iOS identifier is app.ollie.ollie. June-18 audit claims this causes containerURLForSecurityApplicationGroupIdentifier to return None on iOS, silently failing all snapshot writes. Not runtime-verified on a real device since the audit.

summary: Cross-cutting launch-readiness audit of the Ollie monorepo (branch redesign/olive-neumorphic, closed-alpha target).
